overview: President Trump proposed new tariffs of up to 20% on goods from 14 trading partners, including China, Japan and the European Union, after an investigation into industrial overcapacity; China and the EU criticized the plan and China said it could retaliate. The Army detonated its deteriorating stockpile of lead azide at the Iowa ammunition plant on Wednesday and called the operation a success, while scientists and residents said questions about lead contamination remain. A storm forecast to bring damaging wind and heavy rain to New York pushed the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, the first postponement in its history, and a Manhattan judge dismissed landlords' lawsuit against Mayor Zohran Mamdani's rent freeze. Abroad, a fuel tanker crash set off a fire on Cairo's ring road that killed at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

markets.summary: U.S. stock markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving. On Wednesday, stocks fell sharply early as the sell-off in artificial-intelligence companies deepened, then recovered most of the losses by the close: the Nasdaq ended down 0.62% and the Dow rose 0.33%. Two reports landed the same day. The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure, the PCE price index, rose to 3.8% in October from 3.7%, which keeps the Fed on track for a widely expected interest-rate increase in December, and third-quarter economic growth was revised sharply higher. Investors in Asia and Europe largely shrugged off the new U.S. tariff proposals on Thursday, and futures, which trade while the market is closed and hint at where it will open, pointed to gains on Friday.

movers.why: Fell 0.62% on Wednesday after a much steeper early drop in Nvidia, Micron and other AI-related stocks eased before the close; it is still down almost 10% in a month.
Rose 0.33% on Wednesday and stayed above 50,000; the Dow holds fewer AI companies than the Nasdaq, so the tech pullback weighed on it less.
Japan's main index dropped 2.78% on Wednesday, following the Wall Street tech sell-off; outlets reported Asian shares rebounding on Thursday, led by AI stocks.

The average 30-year mortgage rate slipped 7 basis points (0.07 percentage point) to 7.21% this week. The feeds give no single cause, and rates remain high with the Fed expected to raise its benchmark next month.

concept.explanation: A tariff is a tax a government charges on goods brought in from another country. The importer, usually a domestic company, pays it at the border, and then decides how much of the cost to absorb and how much to pass along in higher prices. Governments use tariffs to protect local industries, to raise revenue, or to pressure other countries in trade disputes, and the countries targeted often answer with tariffs of their own. For households, tariffs can show up as higher prices on imported items such as electronics, cars and clothing, and they can feed into inflation, which in turn affects whether the Federal Reserve raises or lowers interest rates.
